notes: Row/bank naming follows the catalogue: bank 't' = rows a-e, bank 'b' = rows f-j. In the picture the rows a-e are the lower half, so the button's lower legs are in 4t.e / 6t.e and its upper legs in 4b.f / 6b.f.

The pushbutton legs are assumed to be at columns 4 and 6, with the two legs in the same column joined internally (side 1 = column 4 connected to 5V, side 2 = column 6 connected to pin 2 and the pull-down resistor); pressing joins the two columns.
The lower power rails in the picture are named bp (red + row) and bn (blue/black - row). Exact rail hole numbers (bp.2, bp.4, bn.2, bn.9) are approximated from the picture.
The resistor sits in row d, columns 6 and 9; the black ground jumper is in 9t.c. The resistor is 10k ohm, entered as value=10000.
The built-in LED on pin 13 is on the Arduino itself and has no external circuit, so there are no edges for it.

The circuit image draws the wires and the two 4.7 kΩ pull-up resistors without showing a breadboard. I used one mini breadboard (bb1) as the junction for the pull-ups and the SDA/SCL joins. The parts list names 2 mini breadboards, but only one is needed, so a second one is not included.

The image shows the reader's pin labelled '3V'. I mapped it to the catalogue port 3V3 on the Nano 33 IoT. The wire from there feeds the pull-up resistors only, because the writer's 3V3 pin is not connected.

In the image, SDA (yellow) joins reader A4 and writer A4, and SCL (teal) joins reader A5 and writer A5. One 4.7 kΩ resistor pulls each line up to 3V3. The teal and yellow lines cross in the drawing, but the small hop shows they are not connected at the crossing.
The 3V3 rail sits on the top positive rail of the breadboard, with the resistor ends at tp.3 and tp.6. These hole positions are arbitrary because the image doesn't specify them.
Both boards are powered and programmed over USB cables from the computer. The usb-cable catalogue entry has no ports, so those edges name only the Nano's USB port.
GND is a single jumper wire between the two boards' GND pins. I used GND.1 on both as an assumption.
The reader/writer sketches and the Serial Monitor screenshot don't add any parts or connections.

items.item: Arduino Nano 33 IoT (or any other Arduino board that supports I2C)

notes: The MKR Zero is not in the catalogue, so it is a new part type. Its pins follow the board silkscreen (D0-D14, A0-A6, VCC (3.3V), 5V, VIN, GND, plus the battery JST and microSD slot).
The manual text says to plug the MKR Zero into the breadboard. The picture shows it beside the breadboard, connected only by jumper wires, and the picture is treated as the authority.
Breadboard columns are estimated from the picture. The DHT22 (RHT03) sits in row a of columns 27-30, in the order VCC, data, NC, GND.

The picture shows the 100 nF capacitor held by two blue wires, so it is modelled as two jumper wires whose far ends are joined to the capacitor leads. The 4.7k pull-up is modelled the same way with two yellow wires, from the VCC strip and the data strip.
The 4.75k resistor in the parts list is given as value 4700. The text says 4k7.
Pin 7 is the data pin per the text. The orange wire is drawn to the header near pin 7.
The microSD card and the LiPo battery are in the picture and the text, so they are included. The battery JST connection is modelled as two wire-end ports.
